chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: Lester hears Jimmy Blanton play Stardust
summary: At the big session Lester, who only praised Slam Stewart, heard Blanton play bowed Stardust and exclaimed over the young bass player.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah, she was in 'Jump for Joy'. That's when Blanton and I were really hanging out together, and earlier, I think I told you about the session, didn't I, with Slam Steward and Jimmy Blanton -- did I tell you about that?

Well, Slam and Pres were really good friends, you know, but Pres didn't know about Blanton, because Blanton and I hung together -- he was my friend. And the picture you saw with Ben Webster and Sonny and Blanton, that's the night that I gave a session, and invited everybody in town -- from the [Bell] Tavern; from all the clubs in town, all the performers,
and that's when Jimmy Luntzwood and Duke Ellington were in town -- but Duke was downtown at the "Jump for Joy".

And that's when everyone had to come up and play -- that's when I really got a big fine for having this, because I wouldn't let the walking delegate in, so that was another mistake I made, if I had let the man in, it would have been all right. Then he thought something was going on wrong, because he wasn't invited. I wouldn't let him in.

But the first time Lester really heard Jimmy Blanton play, because Slam -- he was the man that all the jazz musicians had heard, but Lester was not aware of Blanton. All he used to tell be about was Slam.

I said, "Well, Pres, I want you to hear Jimmy play." And he said, "Little P, you can say what you want to, but my man, Slam, is the baddest." So I said, "Well, you got to hear the Bear". So he hadn't heard Jack the Bear or any of those things, and anyway, this night they came out, and when Sweet Pea was playing piano with that group -- you couldn't see him -- Sweat Pea, Sonny Greer and Ben Webster and Bad Bear Jimmy Blanton.

Well, they played "Stardust", and Jimmy Blanton grabbed the bow and he played "Stardust" and Pres heard him and he said, "Give me a double double!" He says ... "Give me a double double. That little Orrin Tucker done come out here and bruised my man!"
So Bear could play, you know -- Slam could play,
